title: RLPS Control Catalog (.catalog.toml)
description: The jurisdiction-neutral declaration of the control keys one domain's packs may reference, each with a deontic kind and a title. Packs reference these keys; they do not redefine them. A catalog declares that a key EXISTS and what KIND of thing it is - never what any jurisdiction requires. NOT LEGAL ADVICE.

control.description: Control key -> definition. A KEYED object, matching the artifact's [control.<key>] tables, so the key is the table name rather than a field inside a row.

control_key.description: A control key, per spec 2. Enforced HERE via propertyNames because neither layer above can: a `format` facet on a scalar prop is not applied by the N Lang compiler, and nor is a regex prop pattern on the keyed table (both measured 2026-10-26, both pinned as tripwires). A key is matched VERBATIM by a resolver and is long-lived audit evidence in a receipt, so a key differing by case or punctuation is a row no query finds - and under as_configured an unmatched subject fails closed to the caller's whole universe, surfacing as silent over-requiring rather than an error.

catalog_domain.description: Which domain this catalog speaks for.

name.description: The domain name, which spec 2.2 makes the pack FILENAME on disk. A catalog whose name disagrees with its filename validates the wrong domain's packs while every log line names the right one. A schema cannot compare a document to its path, so that agreement is checked by the publishing repository's own test.

description.description: What this domain governs, in one sentence a reviewer reads before the key list.

control_def.description: One control key: what kind of thing it is, and what it names.

kind.description: The deontic kind. A PROHIBITION is subtracted from every resolved set under every posture, so it must never appear in a requirement table - a pack that both requires and forbids a control is not satisfiable. Required rather than defaulted on purpose: a loader that defaults a missing kind turns an omission into an assertion nobody wrote.

title.description: A short human-readable title. Generated pack templates carry it, so an empty one ships into other people's files.

description.description: What the control names, and where its satisfier lives. The catalog is where a reader learns what a key MEANS, because the key itself is opaque.

trigger.description: When the enforcing gate must satisfy it. Deliberately NOT an enum: the set is open, and a closed list here would refuse a domain whose moment this vocabulary has not met.

mechanism.description: A stable name for HOW the control is discharged, for a receipt reader correlating a decision with an enforcement path. A correlation hint, never a contract - and NOT what distinguishes two controls, since a receipt records the control key. Two controls sharing one mechanism is normal and means the path is genuinely shared.

deprecated.description: The date this key was deprecated. A control key is long-lived audit evidence, so a retired key is DEPRECATED rather than deleted: receipts already issued name it, and a reader of one needs it to still resolve. Requires superseded_by - see dependentRequired.

superseded_by.description: What to use instead. Cross-domain successors are spelled <domain>::<key>, because a key is namespaced by its owning domain and a bare name would be ambiguous. An EMPTY list is refused by minItems: it reads as answered, which is worse than absent.

verified_by.description: A reference to the external specification section that defines how this control is verified (e.g. an interoperability spec's anchor). A pointer for a human tracing a control to its defining text, not something a resolver dereferences.

attestation_mode.description: Which attestation mode this control requires, where a domain has more than one and they are NOT interchangeable. Deliberately open rather than an enum: the shipped values are a two-member set in one domain, and closing it here would refuse a domain whose modes this vocabulary has not met. Note what this facet is FOR - two controls may share a mechanism because they discharge through one path while differing in mode, and a receipt that named only the shared mechanism could not tell an auditor which mode was satisfied. The control KEY carries that distinction; this facet records it for a reader.

subject_rights.description: Data-subject rights this control bears on (e.g. withdrawal). Informational: it tells a reviewer which right a control serves, and asserts nothing about whether that right applies in any jurisdiction.

legal_basis_hint.description: A HINT at the consent or processing model a control is usually associated with. The name hedges on purpose and the hedge is load-bearing: a catalog is jurisdiction-neutral and NOT LEGAL ADVICE, so this is a pointer for a human reviewer deciding which packs to author - never a determination, never a basis a resolver may act on, and never evidence that any basis is available anywhere. A resolver MUST NOT vary its decision on this field.
